Bougie
BOO-zhee
adjective (Millennial slang)
Clipped from bourgeois (French, a town-dweller; in Marxist use, the property-owning middle class). In African-American usage from at least the 1960s–70s, bougie (also boujee, bourgie) described someone with upper-class pretensions, putting on airs. Millennials broadened it in the 2010s to anything pretentiously upscale or fancy ("bougie brunch," "bougie candles"), sometimes as self-mockery; the 2016 hit "Bad and Boujee" spread the spelling boujee.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Bougie means fancy in a way that wants to be noticed: the expensive candle, the artisanal brunch, the person who acts above his station. It can be a mild insult or a cheerful confession ("I’m being bougie and getting the good cheese"). The Christian observation: enjoying good things is not a sin, and pretension is. Scripture permits enjoyment of God’s gifts; He "giveth us richly all things to enjoy" (1Ti 6:17). The good cheese is a mercy. But the word’s root idea is putting on airs, presenting oneself as richer or more refined than one is or than others, and Scripture is pointed about it. "There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing: there is that maketh himself poor, yet hath great riches" (Pro 13:7). James rebukes the church that seats the man "with a gold ring, in goodly apparel" in the best place and tells the poor man to stand, "are ye not then partial in yourselves" (Jas 2:4). Paul tells believers, "Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate" (Rom 12:16). The bougie temptation for Millennials was often lifestyle display, curated taste, financed on credit, photographed to signal status. A father teaches his children: enjoy good things with thanks, buy what you can afford, never despise people with less, and never pretend to be more than you are. The truly refined person is the one who makes everyone at the table feel welcome.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial slang (AAVE bougie from bourgeois; 2010s broadening) for pretentiously upscale; enjoying good gifts is allowed (1Ti 6:17), but putting on airs and partiality are not (Pro 13:7; Jas 2:4).

BOUGIE, adj. (AAVE from 1960s–70s; Millennial broadening, 2010s; also boujee, bourgie; clipped from bourgeois) Pretentiously upscale; aspiring to or displaying upper-class taste. "That’s a bougie brunch spot."

No Webster 1828 entry located for the root bourgeois (a French borrowing).

Decode for parents: enjoy good things gratefully; watch for display, debt, and contempt for those with less.

Key Scripture

1Ti 6:17 — "Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy;"

Pro 13:7 — "There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing: there is that maketh himself poor, yet hath great riches."

Jas 2:4 — "Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?"

Rom 12:16 — "Be of the same mind one toward another. Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate. Be not wise in your own conceits."

Pro 16:19 — "Better it is to be of an humble spirit with the lowly, than to divide the spoil with the proud."

Modern Corruption

Bougie names pretension and status display; Scripture allows grateful enjoyment of good gifts and condemns putting on airs and partiality toward the rich.

expand to see more

The corruption is status by consumption. Bougie living, especially when performed online and financed by debt, makes taste a ladder and invites contempt for those lower on it. It is the old sin of pride in a new wardrobe, and the old folly of appearing rich while having nothing. James’s church fell into the same trap when it honoured the gold ring and shamed the poor man.

The recovery is gratitude without pretension. "Better it is to be of an humble spirit with the lowly, than to divide the spoil with the proud" (Pro 16:19). Christians may enjoy good food and beautiful things as gifts, and they should be generous and humble with them: share the good cheese, set an extra place, sit with the lowly. Teach the young that refinement is a matter of manners and kindness, not price tags.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old French borgeis (town-dweller) → bourgeois → Marxist bourgeoisie → AAVE bougie (pretentious) → 2010s Millennial broadening; boujee (2016).

Late Latin burgus (fortified town) → Old French borgeis — a citizen of a town

19th c.: Marxist bourgeoisie — the property-owning middle class

1960s–70s: AAVE bougie — putting on upper-class airs

2010s: Millennial bougie for anything fancy; 2016: "Bad and Boujee"

Biblical anchor: there is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing (Pro 13:7); mind not high things (Rom 12:16)

Usage

""A forty-dollar candle? So bougie.""

"God giveth us richly all things to enjoy (1Ti 6:17); enjoy without airs."

"Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate (Rom 12:16)."
